newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela launches mutual fund in oil industry.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela launches mutual fund in oil industry.

text.p: Venezuela's state-run oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) launched Monday a mutual fund aimed at attracting small investors to the country's oil industry liberalisation.

The fund, called Epic, will be able to take shares in several PDVSA joint-ventures and contracting schemes with foreign and private capital and could be worth at least $500 million, said Eduardo de Lima, head of the PDVSA subsidiary SOFIP which created the scheme.
"Epic will consolidate small investors' savings and channel them into these attractive projects," he said.
The fund will be floated on the Caracas stock exchange early next year after companies have defined their development plans for the third round of operating licences.

Lima said the fund would be independently administered, and would not be guaranteed by PDVSA, although the oil company would retain a 10 percent share through SOFIP. Other shareholders would have a maximum five percent holding.

Epic can take up to 10 percent in each of the 18 operating contracts awarded to foreign and private capital last week, but can also buy five percent in eight profit-sharing contracts awarded in 1995, five to 10 percent in Orinoco extra-heavy crude joint- ventures and five to 20 percent in areas offered in previous operating contract rounds.
Lima said shares in the fund would be allocated to individuals first, and then open to pension funds, other mutual funds and insitutional investors.
Epic would choose where to put its money and would receive dividends from those projects like any other shareholder.
